title: Vintage Photo Collage — An Idea Becomes a Connected System

scenes.title: Cutouts pasted down
scenes.purpose: Assemble the collage: a masthead strip, a torn lightbulb clipping, a newspaper page and two photo prints land on a stationary slate board.
visuals: Stationary slate archival board with fibre grain
Torn masthead strip 'THE DAILY NOTION · No. 44'
Torn halftone lightbulb clipping with tape
Newspaper page with headline and halftone inset
Lift-dependent drop shadows and limited parallax

beats.development: Masthead strip drops in and presses down; lightbulb clipping sweeps in from the upper left, rotating to rest.
Newspaper page slides in from the right and settles carrying 'AN IDEA BECOMES / a connected system'; two photo prints rise from below; tape strips press onto the clipping and page.

scenes.title: Pinned and connected
scenes.purpose: Turn separate fragments into a system: pins pop onto each cutout and a thread draws from pin to pin.
visuals: Tan thread with a slight sag that tightens as each segment reaches its pin
Parallax camera drift settling to rest

beats.development: Pins appear on the bulb and bridge print; first thread runs bulb → bridge print.
Remaining pins appear; thread branches to the gear print, the newspaper column and its inset photo, completing the network.

scenes.title: Settled collage
scenes.purpose: Hold the finished, fully legible collage.
visuals: All cutouts, pins and thread at rest

beats.development: Nothing moves; the headline and connected system are read together.

findings: Headline page is settled by 1.2s, giving about 1.8s of stable reading exposure.
All motion, including parallax drift, is complete by 2.4s, before the 2.7s settle limit.
Card travel durations (0.5–0.64s) follow travel distance; pins and thread are quicker accents.
justifiedHolds: 2.4–3.0s final hold lets the viewer read the headline alongside the finished network.

notes: No optional recipes were supplied; preview demonstrates the primary style (cutouts, paper edges, print halftone, layered parallax) with a refreshed scene-dependent slate board instead of the prior cream canvas.
